knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=2 x + 2 y,\quad v=y + z,\quad w=2 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\left(2 x + 2 y\right) \left(y + z\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):0\le 2 x + 2 y\le 3,\quad 0\le y + z\le 2,\quad 0\le z\le 2\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=2 x + 2 y,\quad v=y + z,\quad w=2 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):0\le u\le 3,\quad 0\le v\le 2,\quad 0\le w\le 4\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)\left(\left(2\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(2\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\left(2 x + 2 y\right) \left(y + z\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(u v\right)\cdot \left|\frac{1}{4}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{u v}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{4}\left(\frac{u v}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left[\frac{u v w}{4}\right]_{w=0}^{w=4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left(\frac{u v \left(4\right)}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{u v \left(0\right)}{4}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left(u v\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\left(u v\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left[\frac{u v^{2}}{2}\right]_{v=0}^{v=2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{u \left(2\right)^{2}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{u \left(0\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(2 u\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(2 u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[u^{2}\right]_{u=0}^{u=3} \\  & =\left(\left(3\right)^{2}\right)-\left(\left(0\right)^{2}\right) \\  & =\left(9\right)-\left(0\right) \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Use the change of variables 

$$
u=- 3 x - 2 y,\quad v=y - z,\quad w=4 z

$$

$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):0\le u\le 2,\quad 0\le v\le 3,\quad 0\le w\le 8\}.

$$

$$

$$

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$
u=x - \frac{y}{3},\quad v=\frac{y}{3},\quad w=\frac{z}{2}
$$

$$

$$

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=x + y^{2},\quad v=y - z,\quad w=4 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\left(y - z\right) e^{x + y^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):0\le x + y^{2}\le 2,\quad 0\le y - z\le 3,\quad 0\le z\le 2\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x + y^{2},\quad v=y - z,\quad w=4 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):0\le u\le 2,\quad 0\le v\le 3,\quad 0\le w\le 8\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)\left(\left(1\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(2 y\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\left(y - z\right) e^{x + y^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(v e^{u}\right)\cdot \left|\frac{1}{4}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{v e^{u}}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{8}\left(\frac{v e^{u}}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left[\frac{v w e^{u}}{4}\right]_{w=0}^{w=8}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{v \left(8\right) e^{u}}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{v \left(0\right) e^{u}}{4}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(2 v e^{u}\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}\left(2 v e^{u}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left[v^{2} e^{u}\right]_{v=0}^{v=3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left(\left(3\right)^{2} e^{u}\right)-\left(\left(0\right)^{2} e^{u}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left(9 e^{u}\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{2}\left(9 e^{u}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[9 e^{u}\right]_{u=0}^{u=2} \\  & =\left(9 e^{\left(2\right)}\right)-\left(9 e^{\left(0\right)}\right) \\  & =\left(9 e^{2}\right)-\left(9\right) \\  & =-9 + 9 e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)\left(\left(1\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(2 y\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=x^{2} + 2 y,\quad v=x + 2 z,\quad w=4 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\sin{\left(x + 2 z \right)} \sin{\left(x^{2} + 2 y \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):\frac{\pi}{2}\le x^{2} + 2 y\le \pi,\quad \pi\le x + 2 z\le 2 \pi,\quad 0\le z\le 1\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x^{2} + 2 y,\quad v=x + 2 z,\quad w=4 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):\frac{\pi}{2}\le u\le \pi,\quad \pi\le v\le 2 \pi,\quad 0\le w\le 4\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2 x & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}2 x & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)\left(\left(2 x\right)\cdot \left(0\right)-\left(2\right)\cdot \left(1\right)\right) \\  & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=- \frac{1}{8}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\sin{\left(x + 2 z \right)} \sin{\left(x^{2} + 2 y \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)\cdot \left|- \frac{1}{8}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{8}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{4}\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{8}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left[\frac{w \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{8}\right]_{w=0}^{w=4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left(\frac{\left(4\right) \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{8}\right)-\left(\frac{\left(0\right) \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{8}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(\left[- \frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \cos{\left(v \right)}}{2}\right]_{v=\pi}^{v=2 \pi}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(\left(- \frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \cos{\left(\left(2 \pi\right) \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \cos{\left(\left(\pi\right) \right)}}{2}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(\left(- \frac{\sin{\left(u \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)}}{2}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(- \sin{\left(u \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[\cos{\left(u \right)}\right]_{u=\frac{\pi}{2}}^{u=\pi} \\  & =\left(\cos{\left(\left(\pi\right) \right)}\right)-\left(\cos{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)}\right) \\  & =\left(-1\right)-\left(0\right) \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$

$$

$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):\frac{\pi}{2}\le x^{2} + 2 y\le \pi,\quad \pi\le x + 2 z\le 2 \pi,\quad 0\le z\le 1\}.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x^{2} + 2 y,\quad v=x + 2 z,\quad w=2 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):\frac{\pi}{2}\le u\le \pi,\quad \pi\le v\le 2 \pi,\quad 0\le w\le 2\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2 x & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}2 x & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)\left(\left(2 x\right)\cdot \left(0\right)-\left(2\right)\cdot \left(1\right)\right) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}

$$

\frac{1}{4}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{2}\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left[\frac{w \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{4}\right]_{w=0}^{w=2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left(\frac{\left(2\right) \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{\left(0\right) \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{4}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(\left[- \frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \cos{\left(v \right)}}{2}\right]_{v=\pi}^{v=2 \pi}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & \right)}}{2}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(\left(- \frac{\sin{\left(u \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)}}{2}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(- \sin{\left(u \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[\cos{\left(u \right)}\right]_{u=\frac{\pi}{2}}^{u=\pi} \\  & =\left(\cos{\left(\left(\pi\right) knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=- 3 x + 3 y,\quad v=y - 2 z,\quad w=3 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\left(- 3 x + 3 y\right)^{2} \left(y - 2 z\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):1\le - 3 x + 3 y\le 3,\quad 1\le y - 2 z\le 4,\quad 1\le z\le 3\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=- 3 x + 3 y,\quad v=y - 2 z,\quad w=3 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):1\le u\le 3,\quad 1\le v\le 4,\quad 3\le w\le 9\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)\left(\left(-3\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(3\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=- \frac{1}{9}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\left(- 3 x + 3 y\right)^{2} \left(y - 2 z\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(u^{2} v\right)\cdot \left|- \frac{1}{9}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{u^{2} v}{9}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\int_{3}^{9}\left(\frac{u^{2} v}{9}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\left(\left[\frac{u^{2} v w}{9}\right]_{w=3}^{w=9}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\left(\left(\frac{u^{2} v \left(9\right)}{9}\right)-\left(\frac{u^{2} v \left(3\right)}{9}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\left(\left(u^{2} v\right)-\left(\frac{u^{2} v}{3}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\left(\frac{2 u^{2} v}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left[\frac{u^{2} v^{2}}{3}\right]_{v=1}^{v=4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{u^{2} \left(4\right)^{2}}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{u^{2} \left(1\right)^{2}}{3}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{16 u^{2}}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{u^{2}}{3}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(5 u^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[\frac{5 u^{3}}{3}\right]_{u=1}^{u=3} \\  & =\left(\frac{5 \left(3\right)^{3}}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{5 \left(1\right)^{3}}{3}\right) \\  & =\left(45\right)-\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) \\  & =\frac{130}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$

$$

$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=- 3 x + 4 y,\quad v=y - z,\quad w=2 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\left(- 3 x + 4 y\right)^{2} \left(y - z\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):1\le - 3 x + 4 y\le 3,\quad 1\le y - z\le 4,\quad 1\le z\le 2\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=- 3 x + 4 y,\quad v=y - z,\quad w=2 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):1\le u\le 3,\quad 1\le v\le 4,\quad 2\le w\le 4\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)\left(\left(-3\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(4\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=- \frac{1}{6}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\left(- 3 x + 4 y\right)^{2} \left(y - z\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(u^{2} v\right)\cdot \left|- \frac{1}{6}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{u^{2} v}{6}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\int_{2}^{4}\left(\frac{u^{2} v}{6}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\left(\left[\frac{u^{2} v w}{6}\right]_{w=2}^{w=4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\left(\left(\frac{u^{2} v \left(4\right)}{6}\right)-\left(\frac{u^{2} v \left(2\right)}{6}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\left(\left(\frac{2 u^{2} v}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{u^{2} v}{3}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\left(\frac{u^{2} v}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left[\frac{u^{2} v^{2}}{6}\right]_{v=1}^{v=4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{u^{2} \left(4\right)^{2}}{6}\right)-\left(\frac{u^{2} \left(1\right)^{2}}{6}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{8 u^{2}}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{u^{2}}{6}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\frac{5 u^{2}}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[\frac{5 u^{3}}{6}\right]_{u=1}^{u=3} \\  & =\left(\frac{5 \left(3\right)^{3}}{6}\right)-\left(\frac{5 \left(1\right)^{3}}{6}\right) \\  & =\left(\frac{45}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) \\  & =\frac{65}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x - \frac{y}{3},\quad v=\frac{y}{3},\quad w=\frac{z}{3}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & - \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & - \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(\left(1\right)\cdot \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{3}\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$

$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x + y^{2},\quad v=y - z,\quad w=4 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$

$$

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):1\le u\le 3,\quad 1\le v\le 2,\quad 4\le w\le 16\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)\left(\left(1\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(2 y\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}

$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

$$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{3}.

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x^{2} + 4 y,\quad v=x + z,\quad w=3 z
$$

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):\frac{\pi}{3}\le u\le \pi,\quad \pi\le v\le 2 \pi,\quad 3\le w\le 12\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=- \frac{1}{12}.

\right)}}{12}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left(\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)-\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{4}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\frac{3 \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\pi}\left(\left[- \frac{3 \sin{\left(u \right)} \cos{\left(v \right)}}{4}\right]_{v=\pi}^{v=2 \pi}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=x^{2} + 3 y,\quad v=x - z,\quad w=4 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\sin{\left(x - z \right)} \sin{\left(x^{2} + 3 y \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):\frac{\pi}{6}\le x^{2} + 3 y\le \pi,\quad \pi\le x - z\le 2 \pi,\quad 1\le z\le 4\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x^{2} + 3 y,\quad v=x - z,\quad w=4 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):\frac{\pi}{6}\le u\le \pi,\quad \pi\le v\le 2 \pi,\quad 4\le w\le 16\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2 x & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}2 x & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)\left(\left(2 x\right)\cdot \left(0\right)-\left(3\right)\cdot \left(1\right)\right) \\  & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=- \frac{1}{12}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\sin{\left(x - z \right)} \sin{\left(x^{2} + 3 y \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)\cdot \left|- \frac{1}{12}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{12}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{4}^{16}\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{12}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left[\frac{w \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{12}\right]_{w=4}^{w=16}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left(\frac{\left(16\right) \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{12}\right)-\left(\frac{\left(4\right) \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{12}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\left(\frac{4 \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}}{3}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\left(\sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\left(\left[- \sin{\left(u \right)} \cos{\left(v \right)}\right]_{v=\pi}^{v=2 \pi}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\left(\left(- \sin{\left(u \right)} \cos{\left(\left(2 \pi\right) \right)}\right)-\left(- \sin{\left(u \right)} \cos{\left(\left(\pi\right) \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\left(\left(- \sin{\left(u \right)}\right)-\left(\sin{\left(u \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\left(- 2 \sin{\left(u \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[2 \cos{\left(u \right)}\right]_{u=\frac{\pi}{6}}^{u=\pi} \\  & =\left(2 \cos{\left(\left(\pi\right) \right)}\right)-\left(2 \cos{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \right)}\right) \\  & =\left(-2\right)-\left(\sqrt{3}\right) \\  & =-2 - \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u={x}^{2}+2y,\,v=x-z,\,w=z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+2y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-z)\,dV,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le {x}^{2}+2y\le 2,\,0\le x-z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,-1\le z\le 1}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u={x}^{2}+2y,\,v=x-z,\,w=z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,-1\le w\le 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2x & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}2x & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-2 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+2y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-z)\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |-\frac{1}{2}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{2}u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,dw\,dv\,du \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}u\,du\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,dv\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}dw \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}]_{u=0}^{u=2}\cdot {[\operatorname{sin}⁡v]}_{v=0}^{v=\pi /2}\cdot [w]_{w=-1}^{w=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2-0)\cdot (1-0)\cdot (1-(-1) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=\frac{2x-y}{2},\,v=\frac{y}{2},\,w=\frac{z}{3}
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}(\frac{2x-y}{2}+\frac{z}{3})\,dV
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le \frac{2x-y}{2}\le 1,\,0\le \frac{y}{2}\le 2,\,0\le z\le 3}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{2x-y}{2},\,v=\frac{y}{2},\,w=\frac{z}{3}
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2,\,0\le w\le 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,\,\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=6.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(\frac{2x-y}{2}+\frac{z}{3})\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}(u+w)\cdot |6|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,(6u+6w)\,dw\,dv\,du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[6uw+3{w}^{2}]_{w=0}^{w=1}\,dv\,du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(6u(1-0)+3({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}))\,dv\,du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(6u+3)\,dv\,du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(6u+3)[v]_{v=0}^{v=2}\,du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(6u+3)\cdot 2\,du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(12u+6)\,du \\  & =[6{u}^{2}+6u]_{u=0}^{u=1} \\  & =6({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})+6(1-0) \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=x+{y}^{2},\,v=y+z,\,w=2z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}(y+z){e}^{x+{y}^{2}}\,dV,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x+{y}^{2}\le 3,\,0\le y+z\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 4}.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x+{y}^{2},\,v=y+z,\,w=2z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 3,\,0\le v\le 1,\,0\le w\le 8}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2y & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(y+z){e}^{x+{y}^{2}}\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}v{e}^{u}\cdot |\frac{1}{2}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{2}v{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{1}{2}v{e}^{u}\,dw\,dv\,du \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{e}^{u}\,du\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}v\,dv\cdot {\int }_{0}^{8}dw \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[{e}^{u}]_{u=0}^{u=3}\cdot {[\frac{{v}^{2}}{2}]}_{v=0}^{v=1}\cdot [w]_{w=0}^{w=8} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{3}-1)\cdot (\frac{1}{2}-0)\cdot (8-0) \\  & =2({e}^{3}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

{∭}_{R}{z}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+3y)\,dV,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}\,2 & 3 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0-(-6)) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
